div.div: Normally, when an app writes data, it goes: App --> to Linux Page Cache (RAM) --> to Filesystem --> to Disk.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 80px; margin-left: 841px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The Problem: Databases like Oracle, MySQL, and Postgres are "smart"—they already have their own internal RAM caches (Buffer Pools). Double-caching in the Linux Page Cache is a waste of memory and CPU.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 358px; height: 1px; padding-top: 170px; margin-left: 841px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The Solution: Using the O_DIRECT flag allows the database to talk directly to the filesystem/disk.

div.div:
Runs as a Deployment on worker nodes (in EKS the control plane is AWS-managed).
They talk to the AWS API. When you ask for a new disk, the Controller calls AWS to CreateVolume. It also handles the "high-level" logic of attaching a volume to an EC2 instance and taking snapshots.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 439px; height: 1px; padding-top: 370px; margin-left: 650px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
As a DaemonSet (one pod on every single worker node).
They perform the Linux-level work. Once AWS attaches a disk to the EC2 instance, the Node pod formats it (e.g., with XFS or ext4) and "mounts" it so your pod can see the folder.

div.div: 1.The Request: You create a PVC.

div.div: 2.The Provisioner: The CSI Controller sees the request and calls the AWS EC2 API to create a physical EBS volume.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: 3. The Attachment: Once the scheduler knows which node the pod will live on, the Controller calls AWS to AttachVolume to that specific EC2 instance.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 273px; height: 1px; padding-top: 450px; margin-left: 1226px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: 4. The Formatting: The CSI Node pod on that specific instance sees the new device (e.g., /dev/nvme1n1). It checks if it has a filesystem; if not, it formats it.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 233px; height: 1px; padding-top: 450px; margin-left: 1546px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: 5.The Mount: Finally, the Node pod mounts the disk into a directory on the host, which is then mapped directly into your running container.
